tldr: A saved allocation list is a statistical resource. The target is the minimum number of actual assignments needed to retain any fixed interior fraction of the published \(n^{-4/3}\) nonlinear minimax gain for a bounded finite-population treatment effect. The proposed theorem establishes linear growth through a frozen signed-Hadamard upper construction and a universal support-only converse valid for every assignment law and all original-record reconstructions. The converse excludes positive second-order gain under every fixed linear budget \(\kappa n\) with \(\kappa\le1\), and for general attaining sequences it requires only \(\liminf m_n/n\ge1\); it does not exclude gain with support \(n+o(n)\). Exact finite certificates compare compressed lists with the full-support benchmark. The coefficient frontier above the fixed budget \(n\), including sublinear excess support, remains open.
